capabilities: Chat with an AI tutor about the selected passage
Ask Socratic counter-questions instead of handing over answers
Generate background deep-dive questions from elsewhere in the book
Write approved edits back into the note with snapshot rollback
Search the web and fetch public pages during conversation
disambiguation: Not a general chatbot or writing assistant; it only tutors on the selected passage and deliberately asks counter-questions instead of giving answers by default.
extras: Desktop only (Obsidian 1.5.0+); the plugin auto-installs a Python sidecar into ~/.socrates-pen/venv from GitHub/PyPI on first enable. API costs are paid through the user's own endpoint; the README documents token billing, privacy boundaries, and troubleshooting. An exercise system is in development and off by default. Manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author wrote a 13,083-line technical manual that only he reads and wanted a companion that has actually read the book and questions you at the point where you stall; the Feynman technique cannot help before you are able to start explaining.
problem: When studying a long technical manual alone, there is no one to ask at the moment you get stuck, and a generic chatbot has not read your book.
